`b10x-spindle`: Run ESS specifications on the capabilities an environment provides. Generated from `crates/spindle-cli/src/cli.rs`.

Exit statuses: `0` success, `1` an error (printed on stderr as `b10x-spindle: …`), `3` admission refused (`admit`, `run`, `play`), `130` or `143` when `play` is stopped by SIGINT or SIGTERM.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`check`](#check) | Compile a specification and print what it declares |
| [`capabilities`](#capabilities) | Print the capabilities a specification, or one component of it, requires, and why |
| [`metrics`](#metrics) | Print the counters an instance of one component reports, derived from the specification |
| [`admit`](#admit) | Admit a specification against an environment: bind every capability or name what is missing |
| [`run`](#run) | Admit a specification, then execute commands read as JSON lines on stdin |
| [`play`](#play) | Play the rally example in this terminal: every component in one process, one tick per period of its periodic binding, the grid redrawn after each |
| [`deploy`](#deploy) | Deploy a specification: place and launch every instance of a placement, collect what they send, and serve the read-only observe API and UI on 127.0.0.1 until SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP |
| [`conform`](#conform) | Run a specification's conformance suite against every component in one process |

## `check`

Compile a specification and print what it declares

```console
b10x-spindle check [OPTIONS] <SPEC>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<SPEC>` | yes |  | The specification directory (holding `system.yaml`) |
| `--json` | no |  | Print JSON instead of text |

## `capabilities`

Print the capabilities a specification, or one component of it, requires, and why

```console
b10x-spindle capabilities [OPTIONS] <SPEC>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<SPEC>` | yes |  | The specification directory |
| `--component <COMPONENT>` | no |  | Only what this component needs when it runs on its own |
| `--json` | no |  | Print JSON instead of text |

## `metrics`

Print the counters an instance of one component reports, derived from the specification.

One line per counter or histogram: its name, its kind and the part of the runtime that measures it.

```console
b10x-spindle metrics [OPTIONS] --component <COMPONENT> <SPEC>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<SPEC>` | yes |  | The specification directory |
| `--component <COMPONENT>` | yes |  | The component |
| `--json` | no |  | Print JSON instead of text |

## `admit`

Admit a specification against an environment: bind every capability or name what is missing.

Prints on stderr one line per outcome the kernel does not run, naming the outcome and what it lacks: a request that selects it is refused, and every other outcome of its command runs. A command the kernel refuses whole (one it cannot select among, or none of whose outcomes runs) is named once instead, as not served. Exits 0 when admitted and 3 when refused.

```console
b10x-spindle admit [OPTIONS] --environment <ENVIRONMENT> <SPEC>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<SPEC>` | yes |  | The specification directory |
| `--environment <ENVIRONMENT>` | yes |  | The `spindle-environment/1` document |
| `--component <COMPONENT>` | no |  | Admit only this component |
| `--json` | no |  | Print JSON instead of text |

## `run`

Admit a specification, then execute commands read as JSON lines on stdin.

Each line is `{"command": "<qualified name>", "input": {...}}`, with an optional `"external": {"<outcome>": true | false}` answering the command's external causes, and an optional `"actor": "<qualified name>"` with `"caller": {"<attribute>": ...}`: the actor the command is sent as and its caller's attributes, every required one of that actor's, which the command reads as `{caller: <attribute>}` and `caller.<attribute>`. Each line prints one JSON result: the outcome with its events and declared error, or a failure. Exits 3, running nothing, when admission is refused. At startup it prints on stderr the same lines `admit` prints for outcomes and commands the kernel does not run.

An external cause the line does not answer is answered by `--decisions`, then by `--answer-default`; one nothing answers fails that line, naming the outcome, and the run goes on.

With `--scenario`, replays an `ess-scenario` document instead of reading stdin: every component in one process on empty in-memory stores, the document read and checked by ESS, its steps run and compared by ESS's conformance runner. Prints what it arranges, each timeline act and each assertion that holds; exits 0 when all hold. At the first that does not, prints it with what was expected and what was observed and exits 1; that replay runs nothing after it. A document ESS refuses, or one of more than 1000 steps, exits 1 before any step runs.

Where a component requires `ingress.network` (`reached_by: network`), runs every component in one process and serves those over HTTP on 127.0.0.1 instead of reading stdin; only `http-loopback` is served, and any other binding exits 1 before listening. Prints `{"listening": "<address>", "components": [...]}` once listening and serves until SIGINT or SIGTERM (exit 130 or 143). Routes are where `ess generate --kind openapi` publishes them: ESS's derived routes, or with `--http` the `ess-http/1` binding's, read and checked by ESS (methods, paths, path variables and per-outcome statuses), an operation it does not name keeping its derived route. A command's body is its input; it answers its outcome's status with the envelope ESS publishes, `{"outcome", "published", "error"?, "payload"?}`, or with the body the binding lists for the outcome: `response` (the command's response alone), `response.<field>` (that field's value alone) or `none` (no body, no `Content-Type`). A view answers `{"rows": [...]}`. Beside those it serves a model console's routes: `GET /api/model` (`{"ir", "subjects"}`, the IR as `ess specify compile --format json` prints it and each outcome's subject), `GET /api/events` (`{"events": [...]}`, every event published so far, in order) and `POST /api/reset` (empties every store, `{"emptied": [...]}`); a route the binding or ESS publishes at one of those paths exits 1 before listening.

A command or view this ingress cannot route (such as a view a binding answers other than as `rows`, or one whose parameter no single query value carries), a command the kernel does not run, and a view the host does not read, keeps its route and answers `501` naming the operation and the construct (with ESS's envelope, `{"refused", "committed": false}`); nothing is read or written for it. Before listening, `run` prints one line on stderr per such operation, in name order: component by component, commands then views, each by qualified name. A run that would serve no operation, one of them an operation this ingress cannot route, exits 1 before listening; one whose operations only the kernel or the host does not run is served as before, each answering `501`.

An outcome the kernel does not run (such as one that generates a value of a type the runtime does not mint), or one this ingress does not answer as the binding lists it (headers, a redirect, the `text` encoding or an error object), refuses only the request that selects it: its command keeps its route and answers every other outcome as declared, and that request answers `501` naming the outcome and what it lacks, with nothing written. Before listening, `run` prints one line on stderr per such outcome. A command none of whose outcomes runs is not served, as above.

A served request carries no `external` object: its external causes are answered by `--decisions`, then by `--answer-default`, each answer per command and outcome, never per input value. A request nothing answers is refused `501`, naming the outcome. Without either flag, a specification that declares an external outcome exits 1 before listening.

`POST /api/reset` may carry a world as its JSON body, each key optional: `{"rows": [{"entity", "identity", "state", "fields"}], "decisions": {...}, "mint": <seed>}`. Every store is emptied, then each row, checked by ESS as a scenario's setup is, written where its entity rests. `decisions`, in the decisions file's shape, answers external causes before `--decisions` and `--answer-default` do, and `mint` seeds every identity and generated value minted, so the same requests mint the same identities; both hold until the next reset. A world that does not validate is refused `400` and changes nothing.

An event binding with `on_failure: retry` runs its command again at once after each attempt that fails, up to 5 attempts, unless `--drop-retries` is given; one with `on_failure: escalate` exits 1 before listening.

```console
b10x-spindle run [OPTIONS] --environment <ENVIRONMENT> <SPEC>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<SPEC>` | yes |  | The specification directory |
| `--environment <ENVIRONMENT>` | yes |  | The `spindle-environment/1` document |
| `--state <STATE>` | no |  | The state file where `store.durable` is bound to `sqlite`, refused otherwise; where `run` serves HTTP, the directory of one state file per component. Without it, state bound to `sqlite` is kept in a temporary directory, printed on stderr and removed when the run ends |
| `--drop-retries` | no |  | Run each event binding that retries on failure (`on_failure: retry`, or a per-refusal policy that retries some refusal) as a `drop` binding: a failed invocation is dropped, not retried. Prints one line per such binding on stderr before listening. Only where `run` serves HTTP |
| `--http <HTTP>` | no |  | An `ess-http/1` binding of the specification's commands and views to methods and paths, JSON or YAML; only where `run` serves HTTP |
| `--port <PORT>` | no |  | The port to serve HTTP on, on 127.0.0.1; `0`, the default, lets the system choose. Only where `run` serves HTTP |
| `--decisions <DECISIONS>` | no |  | A TOML file of answers, `<outcome> = true \| false`, at the top level for every command or under a `["<command>"]` table for one; a command's table wins over the top level |
| `--answer-default` | no |  | Answer every remaining external cause "does not hold" on a command that declares a default branch, so the model selects as it would without it |
| `--fixed-actor <FIXED_ACTOR>` | no |  | Send served commands as this actor (qualified name): a test-backend switch, not authentication; no request proves who sends it. A command that reads its caller is then served instead of answering `501`. Given more than once, each served command is sent as the first fixed actor whose `may:` names it, and a read-granted view read as the first that may read it; one no fixed actor may run is refused `403` "not granted", naming the first, and writes nothing. Each actor and its `--fixed-caller` are checked against the model and printed on stderr, in order, before listening; an undeclared actor or attribute, a required attribute left out, or an actor given twice exits 1. Only where `run` serves HTTP |
| `--fixed-caller <FIXED_CALLER>` | no |  | The caller attributes a fixed actor's commands are sent with, as a JSON object (`{"<attribute>": <value>}`), every required one of that actor's. The n-th `--fixed-caller` is the n-th `--fixed-actor`'s; with several actors each needs its own, `{}` for one that declares no attribute |
| `--scenario <SCENARIO>` | no |  | The `ess-scenario` document to replay |

## `play`

Play the rally example in this terminal: every component in one process, one tick per period of its periodic binding, the grid redrawn after each.

Each component is admitted on its own; exits 3, playing nothing, when one is refused. Opens the match, redraws the grid from the table's `MatchState` view after every tick, and exits 0 once a side has won, printing the winner. State bound to `sqlite` is kept in a temporary directory removed when play ends. A match the model refuses to open, such as one to no points, is an error. SIGINT or SIGTERM stops play, removes the state and exits 130 or 143. Refused and failed commands during play are reported on stderr.

With `--component`, or `SPINDLE_COMPONENT` as the process launcher sets it, plays one component in this process instead, admitted on its own, its bindings carried over TCP: the environment binds `channel` to `tcp`. It listens on `--listen` (`SPINDLE_LISTEN`) for the links its peers open and connects to each component its events lead to at the address in `SPINDLE_PEER_<COMPONENT>`, waiting up to 30 s for it to listen; a peer without one exits 1 naming every such peer and variable, before anything runs. It prints `{"component", "listening", "peers"}` once listening and waits up to 30 s more for a link from each component whose events lead to it; a connection counts as one only once its first message names both ends. Then it prints one JSON line per command it runs, `{"ran", "cause", "outcome"}`. Each command's consequences on every process run before the next tick, so the match is the one a single process plays. The component that accepts `OpenMatch` opens the match, runs the tick, prints `{"view": <MatchState>}` after each and, once a side has won, tells every peer the match is over and exits 0; a peer exits 0 when told by it. A link that closes before that, or a peer that breaks the link protocol (such as one that is not that component saying the match is over), exits 1 naming the peer, and SIGINT or SIGTERM exits 130 or 143, at any point. With `SPINDLE_TELEMETRY` set, it sends its counters there as `spindle-telemetry/1` frames. With the setting `ingress` (`SPINDLE_SETTING_INGRESS`), the loopback address `deploy` gives a component reached over the network, it serves the component's routes there as `run` serves them, refusing a request that does not carry the token in the setting `ingress_token` (as `?t=` or `Authorization: Bearer`) or whose `Host` is not `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`; `ingress` without `ingress_token` exits 1.

```console
b10x-spindle play [OPTIONS] --environment <ENVIRONMENT> <SPEC>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<SPEC>` | yes |  | The rally specification directory |
| `--environment <ENVIRONMENT>` | yes |  | The `spindle-environment/1` document |
| `--target-score <TARGET_SCORE>` | no | `3` | The points a side needs to win |
| `--match-id <MATCH_ID>` | no | `rally` | The identity of the match |
| `--speed <SPEED>` | no | `1` | How many times faster than real time the match clock runs |
| `--component <COMPONENT>` | no |  | Play only this component, its bindings carried over TCP |
| `--listen <LISTEN>` | no |  | The address the component listens on for its peers' links; only with `--component` |

## `deploy`

Deploy a specification: place and launch every instance of a placement, collect what they send, and serve the read-only observe API and UI on 127.0.0.1 until SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP.

The placement is a `spindle-placement/1` document (TOML): its `targets` (`id`, `kind`, `environment`, `ceiling`) and `instances` (`id`, `component`, `target`, `request`, `settings`). Each instance is placed on its target as `spindle.placement.PlaceInstance` decides, its component admitted against `--environment`, whose `name` is the environment a target provides; each one placed is launched by its target's launcher as `b10x-spindle play <spec> --environment <file> --component <component>`, every other component's instance its peer. This build launches `Process` targets; an instance on another kind, or one placement or its launcher refuses, is named on stderr and not run. An instance of a component reached over the network serves its ingress on a loopback address the control process chooses.

Prints `{"listening": "<address>", "url": "http://<address>/?t=<token>"}` once serving. Every request needs the token, as `?t=` or `Authorization: Bearer`, and a `Host` header of `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`; only `GET` is answered. `GET /api/deployment` answers the components, bindings and instances with their state; `GET /api/catalogue?component=` a component's counters; `GET /api/stream` Server-Sent Events, one `sample` per instance per period and one `state` per state change, after the samples of the last 15 minutes; `GET /api/views/<component>/<view>` the view's answer from the ingress of a running instance; `GET /` the observe UI, built into this binary. SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP stops every instance and exits 130, 143 or 129. Each instance is also sent SIGTERM by the system should `deploy` end without stopping it.

```console
b10x-spindle deploy [OPTIONS] --environment <ENVIRONMENT> --placement <PLACEMENT> <SPEC>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<SPEC>` | yes |  | The specification directory |
| `--environment <ENVIRONMENT>` | yes |  | The `spindle-environment/1` document the targets provide |
| `--placement <PLACEMENT>` | yes |  | The `spindle-placement/1` document |
| `--port <PORT>` | no | `7341` | The port to serve on, on 127.0.0.1; `0` lets the system choose |

## `conform`

Run a specification's conformance suite against every component in one process.

The suite is the one ESS synthesises from the specification (`ess conform synthesize`), or the `--suite` file, which must be a suite of this specification. Its scenarios are run by ESS's conformance runner on empty in-memory stores; an `external:` cause holds only where a scenario forces it. Prints every construct the synthesis refused (`refused: refusal[<code>]: ...`) and how many, then `failed <id>` or `error <id>` with what was expected and observed for each executed scenario that did not pass, `skipped <id>: <reason>` for each the target cannot carry out (`unsupported`), and the counts.

Exits 0 when at least one scenario was executed, none ended `error`, every executed scenario passed or failed as `--known-failing` declares, and the `--counts` are held; 1 otherwise, or when the `--suite` is not of this specification; 2 when ESS refuses the declaration; and 3, running nothing, when admission is refused.

```console
b10x-spindle conform [OPTIONS] --environment <ENVIRONMENT> <SPEC>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<SPEC>` | yes |  | The specification directory |
| `--environment <ENVIRONMENT>` | yes |  | The `spindle-environment/1` document |
| `--suite <SUITE>` | no |  | A suite `ess conform synthesize` wrote, instead of synthesising one |
| `--report <REPORT>` | no |  | Where to write the `ess-conformance-report/2`: the counts and every scenario's status |
| `--results <RESULTS>` | no |  | Where to write the `ess-conformance-run/2`: every check of every scenario, with the reason of each that was not carried out |
| `--counts <COUNTS>` | no |  | A `spindle-conformance-counts/1` document: the `executed_scenarios` that execute, and the `skipped` and `known_failed` counts. A held scenario that no longer executes, one that executes and is not held, more skipped or more known failures fails the run, naming each; where the counts moved, the document that holds the run is printed |
| `--known-failing <KNOWN_FAILING>` | no |  | An `ess-known-failures/1` declaration: scenarios this build is known to fail, bound to the exact suite bytes, specification, implementation and build (`sha256:` of `b10x-spindle <version>`), each with its reason and tracking record. Read and accounted by ESS: a declared scenario that failed does not fail the run and is counted `known_failed`; a failure it does not declare still fails it. A declaration that does not bind this run, or names a scenario that passed or ended other than `failed`, exits 2. Requires `--report` and `--accounting-out` |
| `--accounting-out <ACCOUNTING_OUT>` | no |  | Where to write the `ess-known-failure-accounting/1` document |
